newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada cars more efficient but people driving more.
newsitem.headline: Canada cars more efficient but people driving more.

text.p: Canadians' private vehicles have become more fuel efficient but the gains are being wiped out by increased driving, a federal survey released on Thursday showed.
In the fourth quarter 1994 "personal use" vehicles consumed on average 11.8 liters per hundred km, down from 13.8 liters in the fourth quarter 1987, a gain of 14.5 percent.
But the survey, released by Natural Resources Minister Anne McLellan, also showed the the average distance travelled by Canadians rose by 17.2 percent during the period.
"The fact that growth in distance travelled is outpacing improvement in efficiency presents a significant environmental challenge," McLellan said.
